entries.en:
Here is a further update on the Yukiyanagi Building, a few minutes' walk from Hinageshidai Station, which we have covered several times before.
As previously reported, it houses many young IT companies and is popular with young people for its seemingly bright, fresh image.
However, we have once again discovered suspicious activity. When two mysterious giant creatures appeared and confronted one another directly outside, several people were seen entering and leaving the building during the confrontation.
They were not escaping the building out of fear. They deliberately passed beneath the creatures' feet to enter, then came back out a while later.
We have also learned that one of these suspicious figures was carrying a dubious-looking box.
Some suggest they came to retrieve important documents or were simply looting during the disaster. I disagree.
I already know that several companies in the building have business partners whose identities remain stubbornly unclear.
I will continue investigating this matter.

entries.en: The Seven Mysteries of the Yukiyanagi Building: 1
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0065.json:p0/k235; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The Changing Number of Steps in the Yukiyanagi Building

There is a staircase in the Yukiyanagi Building whose number of steps changes.
The emergency stairs connecting the third and fourth floors reportedly have twelve steps at some times and eleven at others.
This is neither a rumor nor an urban legend: actual verification data exists.

Like many readers, I was skeptical and investigated in person.
The result confirmed that it was true.

It is neither an optical illusion nor a trick. The number of steps in the very same staircase really changes.
When there are fewer steps, each becomes slightly taller and deeper, maintaining an uninterrupted staircase.

The mechanism remains unknown, but statistical evidence suggests that the timing of the changes is related to the tides.
We will report again as soon as further information arrives.

entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0065.json:p0/k237; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The Mysterious Floor of the Yukiyanagi Building

As in some other buildings, the Yukiyanagi Building has no "fourth floor."
Its actual fourth floor is designated the fifth.
The elevator has no fourth-floor button either.

Yet there are occasional reports of a fourth-floor button appearing among the elevator buttons.
Those who reported it, however, said they were too frightened to press it.

In fact, there is also information suggesting that one person working in this building suddenly disappears every five years.
Perhaps they merely quit one of its companies without telling anyone.
Still, we cannot rule out the possibility that they disappeared after pressing the fourth-floor button.

entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0065.json:p0/k239; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The Shrine on the Yukiyanagi Building Rooftop

A shrine stands on the rooftop of the Yukiyanagi Building.
Long ago, the building's site was apparently occupied by a merchant's home.

The merchant was skilled at business and traded with members of the upper classes, including samurai families and feudal lords.
But this brought misfortune.

A particularly high-ranking feudal lord took an interest in the merchant's daughter.
He forcibly abducted her to his mansion, then murdered the merchant and his wife, disguising their deaths as the work of bandits to conceal his actions.

As the lord leisurely approached the room where he had confined the daughter, intending to do as he pleased with her, the supposedly murdered merchant suddenly barred his way, covered in blood.
Even when several retainers slashed him, the merchant remained unfazed and bit into the lord's throat, killing him.

With numerous swords and spears piercing his body and a hand and one leg torn off, the merchant nevertheless found his daughter and proudly returned home.
The moment he reached home, he collapsed.
They say that, though murdered, his love for his daughter drove his body onward, and his sheer determination saved her.

His daughter later entered religious life. Moved by his devotion, people built a shrine on the land where his empty house had stood.
Over the years, there were several attempts to remove the shrine, but each brought a succession of mysterious deaths. Even after the building went up, the shrine remained enshrined on its roof.

And, occasionally, a figure believed to be the merchant is said to appear in the offices inside.

entries.en: The Seven Mysteries of the Yukiyanagi Building: 4
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0065.json:p0/k241; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The Mysterious Voices Heard in the Yukiyanagi Building

The following story is whispered about the Yukiyanagi Building.
When someone works alone late at night, the voices of a crowd can supposedly be heard from nowhere.

It happens whenever someone is the only person left on their floor, regardless of which floor it is.
However, once they notice the voices and look around, the sound stops, only to resume when they return to work. Nobody suffers injury or misfortune, but it is an unsettling story nonetheless.

entries.en: The Seven Mysteries of the Yukiyanagi Building: 5
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0065.json:p0/k243; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The Shadow Wandering the Yukiyanagi Building

For some time, there have been numerous reports of something resembling a shadow occasionally crossing the corridors of the Yukiyanagi Building.
The shadow has actually been captured by security cameras, abruptly lending truth to the rumors. Some researchers have reportedly volunteered to investigate.

Early theories suggested it was the lingering resentment of an employee who died from excessive work on one of the floors, or the shadow of the merchant who once lived here, described in Mystery 3. Apparently, neither explanation is correct.

There seem to be no reports of misfortune befalling those who see it, but not knowing what it is makes it deeply unsettling.

entries.en: The Seven Mysteries of the Yukiyanagi Building: 6

entries.en:
The Glowing Floor of the Yukiyanagi Building

Did you know that part of the third-floor corridor in the Yukiyanagi Building lights up once every few years?
Several spots on the tiled floor glow, and stepping on them reportedly changes the color of the light.

One theory holds that stepping on the glowing tiles in a particular order brings good fortune.
Apparently, the only employee to step on them in the correct order, around fifteen years ago, subsequently won first prize in the lottery repeatedly and is now immensely wealthy.
However, nobody has identified this lucky individual, so how much of the story is true remains uncertain.

entries.en: The Seven Mysteries of the Yukiyanagi Building: 7
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0065.json:p0/k247; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The Writing Appearing in the Yukiyanagi Building Windows

Something resembling writing reportedly appears at irregular intervals in the sixth-floor windows of the Yukiyanagi Building.
It cannot be seen from inside the building, only from outside.

The windows have not been tampered with and are regularly cleaned, so the cause is completely unknown.
The writing also appears to be in cursive script, but nobody has deciphered it, leaving its intended message equally mysterious.

Is the building itself trying to communicate something to the outside world? We will report the truth as soon as we discover it.
